# Introduction

Some proteins from the complement system are significantly associated with liver
steatosis. We have also complement system activity information in CHRIS, but
only for the baseline collection not the NAFLD time point. Here we evaluate and
compare the abundance of complement system proteins measured by mass
spectrometry in CHRIS baseline and NAFLD time points. Correlation of abundances
between baseline and NAFLD time point could help justifying the use of
complement system activity information from CHRIS baseline.

# Complement system proteins

The list of proteins part of the complement pathway
[KW-0180](https://www.uniprot.org/keywords/KW-0180) was retrieved from Uniprot
on 2026-10-12. It consists of only (human) reviewed entries.

We first load the CHRIS ScanningSWATH proteomics data.

```{r}
library(tidyfr)

md1 <- data_module(name = "chris_scanningswath_proteins", version = "1.0.0.3",
                   path = DATA_PATH)
prot_data <- data(md1)
prot_ann <- labels(md1)
stopifnot(all(colnames(prot_data) == rownames(prot_ann)))
colnames(prot_data) <- prot_ann$description
rownames(prot_ann) <- prot_ann$description

#' define the columns with protein concentrations
proteins <- rownames(prot_ann)[prot_ann$type != "categorical"]
proteins <- rownames(prot_ann)[prot_ann$Genes != ""]

#' select proteins dataframe
prot_data <- prot_data[, proteins]
```

Next we load the UniProt complement system protein information and restrict to
human proteins.

```{r}
cp <- read.table("data/uniprotkb_keyword_KW_0180_AND_reviewed_2026_10_12.tsv",
                 header = TRUE, sep = "\t", quote = "")
cp <- cp[cp$Organism == "Homo sapiens (Human)", ]
cp <- cp[order(cp$Gene.Names), ]
rownames(cp) <- NULL
```

The table below lists all complement system proteins defined by Uniprot.

```{r, results = "asis"}
library(pander)
pandoc.table(cp[, c("Entry", "Gene.Names")], style = "rmarkdown",
             caption = "Complement system proteins (UniProt).")
```

Next we identify proteins in the ScanningSWATH data set matching the complement
system proteins defined by UniProt. We first match directly using the UniProt
IDs and, for those without a direct match, we evaluate also the UniProt name and
gene names. Note that the latter two did not improve the mapping already
achieved through the UniProt ID.

```{r}
cp$mapped_row <- rep(NA_character_, nrow(cp))
for (i in seq_len(nrow(cp))) {
    ## UniProt ID
    yey <- grep(paste0("(^|;)", cp$Entry[i], "(;|$)"), rownames(prot_ann))
    if (length(yey)) {
        cp$mapped_row[i] <- rownames(prot_ann)[yey]
    } else {
        ## UniProt name
        yey <- which(prot_ann$Protein.Names == cp$Entry.Name[i])
        if (length(yey)) {
            cp$mapped_row[i] <- rownames(prot_ann)[yey]
        } else {
            ## Gene name(s)
            gns <- sub(";", "", unlist(strsplit(cp$Gene.Names[i],
                                                split = " ", fixed = TRUE)))
            yey <- which(prot_ann$Genes %in% gns)
            if (length(yey))
                cp$mapped_row[i] <- rownames(prot_ann)[yey]
        }
    }
}
rownames(cp) <- NULL
```

The complement system proteins measured in the CHRIS ScanningSWATH data set are
listed in the table below.

```{r, results = "asis"}
cp[!is.na(cp$mapped_row), c("Entry", "mapped_row", "Gene.Names..primary.")] |>
    pandoc.table(style = "rmarkdown", caption = "Measured complement proteins.")
```

While the following can not be detected:
`r paste(cp$Gene.Names..primary.[is.na(cp$mapped_row)], collapse = ", ")`

```{r}
cp <- cp[!is.na(cp$mapped_row), ]
```

## Retrieve metadata form CHRIS and NAFLD

We next load metadata from the NAFLD and CHRIS data sets, remove study drop-outs
or individuals without ScanningSWATH proteomics data in either the CHRIS
baseline or NAFLD time point and determine the average time between baseline and
NAFLD sample collection.

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(chrisUtils)
library(nafldData)
library(chrisData)

nd <- nafldData("Personal")
cd <- chrisData("general")

nd <- nd[, c("AID", "aid_chris", "na_examd", "na_age", "na_sex")]
nd$x0_examd <- cd[match(nd$aid_chris, cd$AID), "x0_examd"]
nd$exam_diff <- nd$na_examd - nd$x0_examd
nd$year_diff <- as.numeric(nd$exam_diff, units = "days") / 365

#' Restrict to participants with proteomics data in both time points
nd <- nd[nd$aid_chris %in% rownames(prot_data), ]
nd <- nd[nd$AID %in% rownames(prot_data), ]

quantile(nd$year_diff)
```

Note: from the 327 NAFLD participants we reduce to `r nrow(nd)` that have
proteomics data for both the baseline **and** NAFLD time point.

### Change in phenotype data between baseline and NAFLD

We next load also the (clinical) phenotype data for the participants (defined in
*nafld_data_overview.Rmd*).

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(readxl)
mp <- read_excel(file.path("data", "masld_phenotypes.xlsx")) |>
    as.data.frame()
rownames(mp) <- mp$AID
colnames(mp) <- paste0("na_", colnames(mp))

nd <- data.frame(
    nd,
    mp[nd$AID, c("na_case", "na_BMI", "na_body_fat", "na_visc_fat",
                 "na_HbA1c", "na_liver_stiffness", "na_liver_fat",
                 "na_visual_fat", "na_T2D", "na_waist_circumference",
                 "na_triglycerides", "na_sld_type", "na_MetS", "na_med_DM",
                 "na_med_BP", "na_med_lip", "na_med_MS")],
    check.names = FALSE)
nd$na_sld_type <- factor(nd$na_sld_type, levels = c("none", "MASLD",
                                                    "MetALD", "SLD"))

#' Add respecive information (if available) also from CHRIS baseline.
#' BMI, fat
tmp <- chrisData("clinical")
rownames(tmp) <- tmp$AID
nd$x0_BMI <- tmp[nd$aid_chris, "x0an03a"]
nd$x0_BMI <- as.numeric(sub(">", "", nd$x0_BMI))
nd$x0_body_fat <- tmp[nd$aid_chris, "x0an04"]
nd$x0_body_fat <- as.numeric(sub(">", "", nd$x0_body_fat))
nd$x0_visc_fat <- tmp[nd$aid_chris, "x0an05"]

#' triglycerides, glucose, HbA1c
tmp <- chrisData("Labdata")
rownames(tmp) <- tmp$AID
nd$x0_HbA1c <- tmp[nd$aid_chris, "x0lp06a"]
nd$x0_triglycerides <- tmp[nd$aid_chris, "x0lp19"]

#' medication summary from baseline
tmp <- chrisData("drugs_summary")
rownames(tmp) <- tmp$AID
nd$x0_med_DM <- tmp[nd$aid_chris, "x0dd21"]
nd$x0_med_BP <- tmp[nd$aid_chris, "x0dd20"]
nd$x0_med_lip <- tmp[nd$aid_chris, "x0dd22"]
nd$x0_med_MS <- tmp[nd$aid_chris, "x0dd23"]

#' calulating differences
nd$diff_BMI <- nd$na_BMI - nd$x0_BMI
nd$diff_body_fat <- nd$na_body_fat - nd$x0_body_fat
nd$diff_visc_fat <- nd$na_visc_fat - nd$x0_visc_fat
nd$diff_HbA1c <- nd$na_HbA1c - nd$x0_HbA1c
nd$diff_triglycerides <- nd$na_triglycerides - nd$x0_triglycerides
```

We visualize the changes in several key variables through a heatmap.

```{r, fig.cap = "Heatmap grouping participants based on changes observed in variables between NAFLD and CHRIS baseline collection. Note: colors are capped at 5, the changes in the first 2 rows are between -8 and -10.", fig.height = 18, fig.width = 7}
library(RColorBrewer)
library(pheatmap)
m <- as.matrix(nd[, c("diff_BMI", "diff_body_fat", "diff_visc_fat",
                      "diff_HbA1c", "diff_triglycerides")])
m <- scale(m, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE) # scale COLUMNS (traits)
rownames(m) <- nd$AID
ann <- nd[, c("na_sex", "na_med_DM", "na_med_lip", "year_diff", "na_age")]
rownames(ann) <- nd$AID

#' Note:
#' no relationship with na_sld_type

#' Symmetric color palette
col_pal <- colorRampPalette(rev(brewer.pal(n = 7, name = "RdYlBu")))(100)
brks <- seq(-5, 5, length.out = 101)

pheatmap(m, annotation_row = ann, color = col_pal, breaks = brks)
```

There are some groups or participants with an increase in body fat or HbA1c
measurements. This seems to be unrelated to the participant's age, sex or
difference between baseline and NAFLD collection time point. Individuals with
T2D medication (at NAFLD time point!) seem however enriched among those with the
largest changes. Also, single individuals seem to have drastic differences for
single variables (in particular the first two rows). We might eventually
identify and flag/remove these participants from some of the following analyses.

We also identify participants for which medication changed between baseline and
NAFLD time point (ignoring missing values, i.e., considering **only changes from
Yes -> No and No -> Yes**).

```{r}
med_change <- nd$x0_med_DM == "Yes" & nd$na_med_DM == "No" |
    nd$x0_med_DM == "No" & nd$na_med_DM == "Yes" |
    nd$x0_med_BP == "Yes" & nd$na_med_BP == "No" |
    nd$x0_med_BP == "No" & nd$na_med_BP == "Yes" |
    nd$x0_med_lip == "Yes" & nd$na_med_lip == "No" |
    nd$x0_med_lip == "No" & nd$na_med_lip == "Yes" |
    nd$x0_med_MS == "Yes" & nd$na_med_MS == "No" |
    nd$x0_med_MS == "No" & nd$na_med_MS == "Yes"
med_change <- which(med_change)
```

```{r, results = "asis"}
## Note: no change in med_MS
tmp <- nd[med_change, c("na_age", "year_diff", "x0_med_DM", "na_med_DM",
                        "x0_med_BP", "na_med_BP", "x0_med_lip", "na_med_lip",
                        "diff_BMI", "diff_body_fat",
                        "diff_HbA1c", "diff_triglycerides")]
tmp$med_DM <- tmp$na_med_DM
tmp$med_DM[tmp$x0_med_DM == tmp$na_med_DM] <- ""
tmp$med_lip <- tmp$na_med_lip
tmp$med_lip[tmp$x0_med_lip == tmp$na_med_lip] <- ""
tmp$med_BP <- tmp$na_med_BP
tmp$med_BP[tmp$x0_med_BP == tmp$na_med_BP] <- ""
pandoc.table(tmp[, c("na_age", "year_diff", "diff_BMI", "diff_body_fat",
                     "diff_HbA1c", "diff_triglycerides", "med_DM", "med_BP",
                     "med_lip")], style = "rmarkdown", split.table = Inf,
             caption = paste0("Individuals with a change in reported ",
                              "medication. Yes means a change from No to Yes,",
                              " No from Yes to No (baseline to NAFLD)."))
```

We repeat the heatmap with trait changes including the information whether
participants changed medication.

```{r, fig.cap = "Heatmap grouping participants based on changes observed in variables between NAFLD and CHRIS baseline collection. Note: colors are capped at 5, the changes in the first 2 rows are between -8 and -10. Row annotations indicate changes in medication.", fig.height = 18, fig.width = 7}
ann_med <- data.frame(BP = rep(NA_character_, nrow(nd)),
                      DM = rep(NA_character_, nrow(nd)),
                      LL = rep(NA_character_, nrow(nd)))
ann_med$DM[which(nd$x0_med_DM == "No" & nd$na_med_DM == "Yes")] <- "Yes"
ann_med$DM[which(nd$x0_med_DM == "Yes" & nd$na_med_DM == "No")] <- "No"
ann_med$BP[which(nd$x0_med_BP == "No" & nd$na_med_BP == "Yes")] <- "Yes"
ann_med$BP[which(nd$x0_med_BP == "Yes" & nd$na_med_BP == "No")] <- "No"
ann_med$LL[which(nd$x0_med_lip == "No" & nd$na_med_lip == "Yes")] <- "Yes"
ann_med$LL[which(nd$x0_med_lip == "Yes" & nd$na_med_lip == "No")] <- "No"
rownames(ann_med) <- nd$AID

pheatmap(m, annotation_row = ann_med, color = col_pal, breaks = brks)
```

The observed changes for some of the traits seem mostly unrelated to the
(reported) change in medication.

We also evaluate which trait could be used as a proxy for steatosis (*liver fat*
variable).

```{r}
lf_proxy <- lapply(
    c("na_body_fat", "na_visc_fat", "na_HbA1c", "na_triglycerides", "na_BMI"),
    function(x) {
        data.frame(x = x, y = "na_liver_fat",
                   r = cor(nd[, x], nd[, "na_liver_fat"],
                           use = "pairwise.complete.obs", "pearson"),
                   rho = cor(nd[, x], nd[, "na_liver_fat"],
                             use = "pairwise.complete.obs", "spearman"))
    }) |> do.call(what = rbind)
```

```{r, results = "asis"}
pandoc.table(
    lf_proxy, style = "rmarkdown",
    caption = "Correlation of various traits with steatosis in NAFLD.")
```

The *best* correlating variables are BMI and visceral fat. Note that this was
calculated on only `r nrow(nd)` participants. Increasing to the full data set
might change the values a bit. The correlations are however not large enough to
justify using that variable as a proxy for steatosis in the baseline.

### Evaluating complement system protein abundances in baseline and NAFLD

We next subset the proteomics data sets to the complement system proteins and
data for the selected participants.

```{r}
prot_baseline <- prot_data[nd$aid_chris, cp$mapped_row]
prot_nafld <- prot_data[nd$AID, cp$mapped_row]
```

We first inspect the data using unsupervised methods such as PCA and HCL.

```{r, fig.cap = "Heatmap of complement system protein abundances in CHRIS baseline and NAFLD time point.", fig.height = 20, fig.width = 7}
prot_comb <- rbind(prot_baseline, prot_nafld)
colnames(prot_comb) <- cp$Gene.Names

ann_rows <- data.frame(T = rep("NAFLD", nrow(prot_comb)))
ann_rows$T[seq_len(nrow(prot_baseline))] <- "baseline"
rownames(ann_rows) <- rownames(prot_comb)

pheatmap(scale(prot_comb), annotation_row = ann_rows)

```

The data does not separate by time points suggesting that there is no systematic
difference in complement system proteins between CHRIS baseline and NAFLD time
point.

Evaluating protein abundances using a PCA.

```{r, fig.width = 14, fig.height = 7}
lbls <- c(seq_len(nrow(prot_baseline)), seq_len(nrow(prot_baseline)))

pc_all <- prcomp(scale(prot_comb, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE))
library(CompMetaboTools)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3, 1.5), cex.lab = 1.3)
plot_pca(pc_all, pch = 21, col = "#000000ce", labels = lbls)
plot_pca(pc_all, pch = 21, col = "#000000ce",
         pc_x = 3, pc_y = 4, labels = lbls)
```

Not clear and easy to interpret. Some sample pairs baseline-NAFLD seem to group
closely.

Evaluating the average abundance across individuals between the two time points.

```{r, fig.cap = "Comparison of the mean abundance of complement system proteins across participants for the two sampling time points."}
library(vioplot)
vioplot(data.frame(
    baseline = colMeans(prot_baseline),
    nafld = colMeans(prot_nafld)))
grid()
```

The mean abundance of complement system proteins across the individuals in the
two sampling time points are comparable, with a slight lower abundance in the
NAFLD time point.

The questions are:

- Are the abundances of complement system proteins correlated between baseline
  and NAFLD collection?
- Are abundances systematically different for some proteins?
- Are there individuals with constant and others with differences in complement
  system protein abundances?

### Correlation of complement protein abundances between baseline and NAFLD time point

To address the first question we calculate the correlation of complement system
proteins between time points and fit in addition per-protein linear models
comparing the abundances.

```{r}
cp_corr <- lapply(colnames(prot_baseline), function(x) {
    r <- cor(prot_nafld[, x], prot_baseline[, x])
    l <- lm(y ~ x, data.frame(y = prot_nafld[, x], x = prot_baseline[, x]))
    l <- summary(l)
    data.frame(UniProt = x,
               R = r,
               coef = l$coefficients[2L, "Estimate"],
               p.value = l$coefficients[2L, 4L])
}) |> do.call(what = rbind)
cp_corr$p.adj <- p.adjust(cp_corr$p.value, method = "bonferroni")
cp_corr$Gene.Names <- cp$Gene.Names[match(cp_corr$UniProt, cp$mapped_row)]
```

Abundance correlations between baseline and NAFLD time point for complement
system proteins are listed below (ordered by significance).

```{r, results = "asis"}
cp_corr[order(cp_corr$p.value),
          c("UniProt", "Gene.Names", "R", "coef", "p.adj")] |>
    pandoc.table(
        style = "rmarkdown", row.names = FALSE, split.table = Inf,
        caption = paste0("Correlation of complement system protein abundances ",
                         "between NAFLD and CHRIS baseline sampling."))
```

There is correlation for some complement system protein abundances between NAFLD
collection and CHRIS baseline. The slopes for the individual models are all
smaller 1 suggesting on average slightly **lower** abundances in the NAFLD
collection. Whether these correlations are strong enough to justify using
baseline complement activation data is questionable.

```{r, fig.cap = "Correlation of protein abundances between NAFLD and CHRIS baseline collection for two example complement system proteins.", fig.width = 14, figh.height = 7}
col_sex <- ifelse(nd$na_sex == "Female", "#E41A1C", "#377EB8")
plot_corr <- function(x, col, ...) {
    d <- data.frame(y = prot_nafld[, x], x = prot_baseline[, x])
    bg <- paste0(col, 80)
    bg[is.na(col)] <- NA
    plot(d$x, d$y, xlim = range(d), ylim = range(d),
         main = paste0(x, ": ", cp$Gene.Names[match(x, cp$mapped_row)]),
         xlab = expression(log[2]~abundance~baseline),
         ylab = expression(log[2]~abundance~NAFLD), pch = 21,
         col = col, bg = bg, ...)
    grid()
    abline(0, 1, lty = 3, col = "grey")
    l <- lm(y ~ x, data = d)
    abline(l)
}


par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot_corr("P01024", col_sex)

plot_corr("P06681", col_sex)

#' check different traits
## library(scales)
## col_fun <- col_numeric(brewer.pal(7, "Set1")[6:7],
##                        domain = range(nd$na_BMI, na.rm = TRUE))
## plot_corr("P01024", col_fun(nd$na_BMI), cex = 2)
## col_fun <- col_numeric(brewer.pal(7, "Set1")[6:7],
##                        domain = range(nd$na_HbA1c, na.rm = TRUE))
## plot_corr("P01024", col_fun(nd$na_HbA1c), cex = 2)
## col_fun <- col_numeric(brewer.pal(7, "Set1")[6:7],
##                        domain = range(nd$na_visc_fat, na.rm = TRUE))
## plot_corr("P01024", col_fun(nd$na_visc_fat), cex = 2)
## tmp <- nd$diff_visc_fat
## col_fun <- col_numeric(brewer.pal(7, "Set1")[6:7],
##                        domain = range(tmp, na.rm = TRUE))
## plot_corr("P01024", col_fun(tmp), cex = 2)


```

For a subset of participants, the correlation for C3 protein abundances would
even be higher. We could however not identify an obvious variable that could
characterize those.

### Pairwise correlation of complement protein abundances for the same individual

We next calculate pairwise correlation of complement system protein abundances
in baseline and NAFLD time point for each individual. We can evaluate a) whether
correlation between samples of the same individual are on average higher than
between random pairs and we can b) identify individuals with high and those with
low correlations. The latter might be excluded from an analysis evaluating
complement system activity in baseline.

```{r}
calc_cor <- function(x, y) {
    res <- numeric(nrow(x))
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(x)))
        res[i] <- cor(as.numeric(x[i, ]), as.numeric(y[i, ]))
    res
}

#' Calculate (pearson) correlation between pairs of samples of the same
#' participant
cor_self <- calc_cor(prot_baseline, prot_nafld)

#' Calculate correlation for random pairs, 1000 times.
set.seed(123)
nr <- nrow(prot_nafld)
cor_rand <- replicate(
    1000, calc_cor(prot_baseline, prot_nafld[sample(seq_len(nr)), ]),
    simplify = FALSE)
cor_rand <- do.call(cbind, cor_rand)
cor_rand_mean <- rowMeans(cor_rand)
```

The distribution of per-participant pairwise protein abundances between baseline
and NAFLD time point are shown below in addition to the average correlation
between 1000 random participation pairs.

```{r, fig.cap = "Distribution of per-participant complement system protein correlations between baseline and NAFLD time point (blue) and average correlation between 1000 random pairs (black)."}
plot(density(cor_self), xlab = "correlation", main = "", ylim = c(0, 11),
     col = "#0000ff80", lwd = 2)
points(density(cor_rand_mean), type = "l", col = "#00000080", lwd = 2)
grid()
```

The correlation is significantly higher for paired samples. There is also an
interesting bump in the distribution (partially present also in the background
distribution). Testing whether this difference is significant using a Student's
t-test:

```{r}
t.test(cor_self, cor_rand_mean)
```

The pairwise correlations seem to be unrelated to any of the main study
covariates.

```{r}
cls <- c("year_diff", "na_BMI", "na_age", "na_body_fat", "na_visc_fat",
         "na_HbA1c", "na_liver_stiffness", "na_waist_circumference",
         "na_triglycerides", "diff_BMI", "diff_body_fat",
         "diff_visc_fat", "diff_HbA1c", "diff_triglycerides")
tmp <- lapply(cls, function(z) {
    cor(x = cor_self, y = nd[[z]], use = "pairwise.complete.obs",
        method = "spearman")
})

## *Best* correlations...
plot(cor_self, nd$year_diff)
```

Still, maybe interesting to evaluate the worst correlations.

```{r, results = "asis"}
idx <- order(cor_self)
nd$cs_cor <- cor_self

tmp <- nd[idx, c("cs_cor", "na_age", "na_sex", "year_diff", "na_BMI",
                 "na_T2D")][1:10, ]
pandoc.table(
    tmp, style = "rmarkdown",
    caption = paste0("Top 10 participants with the lowest correlation of ",
                     "complement system protein abundances between baseline ",
                     "and NAFLD time point"))
```

We could exclude these participants from an analysis on the complement system
activity ... eventually.

sessionInfo()
